title: Spearman rank correlation
biology: Microbial ecologists compare soil salinity with bacterial richness across independent soil cores.
design: Forty-five independent sites contribute one salinity and richness measurement each.
other_examples: Ordinal condition score and body size
question: Does bacterial richness tend to decline as salinity increases?
null: The population Spearman rank correlation is zero.
options: exact = FALSE handles tied richness values
Choose a one-sided alternative only before seeing the data
assumptions: Monotonic association is the target; zero does not rule out every pattern
parametric: Model the curved mean relationship directly if prediction is needed
A suitable transformation may linearize the mean
nonparametric: Spearman reduces the influence of extreme magnitudes
Nonmonotonic patterns require a different model or question

plot_args.note: Name the original variables, not their ranks
Keep the point size readable in a lecture room

practice: Does rho tell you how many taxa are lost per additional ppt of salinity?
code_simulate:
set.seed(1113)
salinity <- runif(45, .5, 8)
richness <- round(90 - 25 * log(salinity + 1) + rnorm(45, 0, 7))
d <- data.frame(site = 1:45, salinity_ppt = salinity, richness = richness)
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
plot(d$salinity_ppt, d$richness, pch = 21, bg = "#73649A", col = "white",
     cex = 1.4, xlab = "Soil salinity (ppt)", ylab = "Bacterial richness (taxa)")
code_analysis:
fit <- cor.test(d$salinity_ppt, d$richness,
                method = "spearman", exact = FALSE,
                alternative = "two.sided")
generating_model: 45 independent site salinities are Uniform(0.5, 8). Richness is 90 - 25*log(salinity + 1) + Normal(0, 7 SD) noise, rounded to the nearest taxon.
generating_truth: The underlying mean response decreases nonlinearly with salinity, creating a negative monotonic association. No fixed numeric population Spearman coefficient was specified.
teaching_point: Ranks can summarize a monotonic curve without claiming a constant change in the original response units.
